title: The Israelites: Race In The Bible

sense.text:
“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” This is Christ speaking to a heathen woman, telling her he is not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. That is who he said he was sent to get.

There is a doctrine going around from the modern satanic Christians that the Israelites were not a race. There is an underhanded reason behind it. It is clear the Messiah was sent to a particular group of people. If you make that people no longer a nation, then he saved everyone, because he wasn’t sent to a particular race of people. So the plot is to make Israel not a nation at all, so it can appear as if he was sent to save everyone. Very slick. You see through it; you’re not fooling anybody. Edom, we know what you’re doing. It doesn’t work.

It is understandable why that doctrine is pushed: they are desperate, hoping that God is going to come and save them when he’s not.

precepts.why:
“For the Son of man is come to save” that which is lost. For some odd reason, in many revised version Bibles Matthew 18:11 is removed entirely: they go from verse 10 and skip to verse 12. They removed 11 altogether. Why?

Because here he explains who he was sent to save: that which is lost. Who is lost? The lost sheep of the house of Israel, Matthew 15:24. Take Israel away as a people and you take away who he came for.

sense.text:
Moses says, “Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you”. The God of who? Of your fathers. Your fathers go back to your progenitor, your originator, your predecessor. That’s what a father is.

All these words, genealogy, a line of descent, ancestors, forefathers, progenitors, family tree, bloodline, pedigree, stock, house, generation, are in the Bible regarding the children of Israel. If Israel were not a race you should not find the word descent in the Bible at all, nor ancestor, nor any of these. Is the house of Israel not written in the Bible numerous times? Yet somehow they say the children of Israel are not a race of people. And that is all to push the idea that those people over there, those bastards who call themselves Israelites, are Israelites, because they try to say anyone could be a Jew through conversion. Very slick.

“Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel”. That part alone: the children of Israel. Israel had children. So the children of Israel is a race of people: the children of a man. That is what the race is. Lineage.
“The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”: your fathers again. “This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.”

“The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, appeared unto me”. So the fathers are Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Those are our progenitors, the line the children of Israel descend from.

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them”: that means idols. “For I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”.

Fathers generate children. The iniquity of the fathers upon the children: children of who? Children of the fathers. That’s a generation. You have a grandfather, a father and a grandson: first, second and third, that’s generations. That’s a lineage. Not to be a race, you cannot have these things. How could Israel not have them? It doesn’t make any sense.

“Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children”: generations, “unto the third and to the fourth generation.” That is lineage; these are descendants. Once again it is clear.

sense.text:
“Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers”. By the house of who? Of their fathers. That goes back to the family tree, and the house is in the definition of ancestors too. Your house comes from your father. That is why it is called the house of Israel; the children of Israel is from your father.

Another doctrine is that both your parents have to be Israel for you to be Israel: if your mother or father is a heathen, you’re a heathen. That is an Israeli Edomite doctrine. It is not biblical whatsoever. The Israelis, the Edomite Jews, … the fake ones, the cave Jews, push that nonsense: according to your mother is your nationality, and if your father or mother is a heathen you’re not a Jew, you’re a bastard. That’s not in the Bible. And you have Israelites repeating that same nonsense, meanwhile they can’t go back five generations, which is insane.

precepts.why: “And with you there shall be a man of every tribe; every one head of the house of his fathers.” The house of his fathers.
“These were the renowned of the congregation, princes of the tribes of their fathers, heads of thousands in Israel.” The tribes of their fathers: here we go with the father again.

“And they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers”. They declared their pedigrees: the line of descent, after their families. Families is in the verse, and family, house and stock are all with genealogy.

Most of the time you hear pedigree regarding animals, like a bulldog or a terrier, showing it to be pure bred. It is also the recorded ancestry, and that recording is the Bible, especially of the upper class, and we know the whole nation of Israel is upper class above all the nations on the earth. Pedigree is the background of a person as conferring distinction or quality, and Israel is distinct and has more quality than all nations on the earth. So is pedigree in the Bible? Yes. Does pedigree refer to Israel? Yes.

The pedigree is based upon the house of your father. The children of Israel, their pedigree is based upon their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not mothers, because a man carries the seed. The seed is placed in a woman and it grows within the woman, but the seed still belongs to the man.
“And the children of Reuben, Israel’s eldest son, by their generations, after their families, by the house of their fathers”. So the Reubenites were declared based upon their father.
“Of the children of Simeon, by their generations, after their families, by the house of their fathers”: the same thing again.
“Of the children of Gad, by their generations, after their families, by the house of their fathers”.

“Of the children of Judah, by their generations, after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all that were able to go forth to war”. When you read it, it is the same thing regarding each tribe: based upon the house of their fathers. It is redundant on purpose, to make it clear.

sense.text: “Go in and possess the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers”: unto who? Your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “to give unto them and to their seed after them.” Unto their what? Their seed after them: their descendants. And the seed comes from the males.

precepts.why:
“When the Lord thy God shall have brought thee into the land which he sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give thee great and goodly cities, which thou buildedst not”. We keep reading over and over again about our fathers, our fathers, our fathers; it’s nonstop.

The nation of Israel had a line of descent. They had a lineage, a bloodline, a family tree; therefore they had to be a race. It’s madness to say otherwise.

sense.text:
Let’s see if ancestor is in the Bible; maybe it’s not, because after all Israel somehow is not a race. “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Of their who? Their ancestors. “Whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the heathen, that I might be their God: I am the Lord.”

He is remembering our ancestors, whom he took out of the land of Egypt. Those ancestors who came out of Egypt had children; they generated children, and that gives you generations, genealogies, descendants. It is clear.

That shouldn’t be in the Bible either, because somehow we’re not a race. “Jest not with a rude man”: don’t play around with a rude man, “lest thy ancestors be disgraced.” You bring a bad name to yourself, and you disgrace your ancestors. Ancestry, in the Bible, once again.

Of old time there was a house negro who wanted position and authority, and he decided to slander his brothers in order to gain that authority. You have them on YouTube too, and you used to have one up in here who is now gone.

This man “had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles”. He defiled himself willingly; he gave in. He wasn’t forced. He wanted to fall behind white folks: he loved white folks, he loved the Greeks. “Nor have any more access to the holy altar”, because he was of the priestly line.

“Howbeit, having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprize”: to gain position as high priest. Called into counsel and asked how the Jews stood affected and what they intended, he answered that those “whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war, and are seditious”. So he is slandering them.

“Therefore I, being deprived of mine ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither”. Being deprived of what? His ancestors’ honour, which was the Levitical priesthood. He is referring to his priesthood regarding his ancestry, the Levitical line. But the key word here is ancestors. Even our wicked forefathers used the term. Ancestors is in the Bible.

Let’s see if the heathens outside of Israel knew Israel was a race. Maybe they didn’t; maybe they were confused. This is the time of the general of Nebuchadnezzar, when he was seeking knowledge of the nations he was trying to conquer, seeking information regarding our nation, and this heathen gave him intel regarding our people. He was “the captain of all the sons of Ammon”: he was an Ammonite. “I will declare unto thee the truth concerning this people”.

“This people are descended of the Chaldeans”. What is he talking about? We are not Chaldeans. He means they descended from a man who came out of there: he is talking about Abraham, who resided in Ur of the Chaldees, which is modern day Iraq.

“They would not follow the gods of their fathers, which were in the land of Chaldea.” He refused the gods of his fathers: that is Abraham, because his family members were wicked as hell, including his father.

“For they left the way of their ancestors, and worshipped the God of heaven, the God whom they knew”. That is about Abraham. “And they fled into Mesopotamia, and sojourned there many days”: that is Haran.

So even the heathen knew this people by their descent and their ancestors. Reading about our forefathers all throughout the Bible, yet somehow they’re not a race.

precepts.why: “They went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees”: that’s where Abraham and them came from, “to go into the land of Canaan”. The Lord promised Abraham land, and Abraham believed and he left: he left with his father, his wife and his nephew, and Lot’s family as well. “And they came unto Haran, and dwelt there.” That is Mesopotamia as well. So the people descended of the Chaldeans means descended of Abraham, who came out of there.

This gives more detail. “And it happened, that when they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, and had gotten them many children”: this is when the earth was replenished after the flood. Generations. They “were a great people, they began again to be more ungodly than the first”: worse than those who were killed by the flood.

“Now when they lived so wickedly before thee, thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham. Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will”: his commandments. “And madest an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed.”

“And unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac also thou gavest Jacob and Esau. As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau”: he put Esau away, I’ll deal with you. “And so Jacob became a great multitude.” So the Ammonite in Judith was referring to Abraham, chosen out from among the ungodly, who left the way of his ancestors.

“Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time”, even the father of Abraham, “and they served other gods.” They served what? Other gods. It goes back to what was said in Judith: they would not follow the gods of their fathers.

“And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac.” Abraham’s father served other gods. That is why, before Abraham went on to the promised land, his father died: I’m not bringing him with you, that dude’s a pagan. He dropped dead, and Abraham left Haran, left his dead father over there, and moved to Canaan. His father was a pagan like all the rest of his family, unlike Abraham, who was not.

sense.text: “If there be any error in this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them.” He is telling the general their strengths and weaknesses: if they sin against their God, we can beat them. If they are keeping the commandments, we can’t touch them; they are untouchable.

“But if there be no iniquity in their nation, let my lord now pass by, lest their Lord defend them, and their God be for them, and we become a reproach before all the world”: we get destroyed.

In their what? In their nation. Look at that word nation: its land, in our case, is Jerusalem, and one of the words that means nation is race. So nation and race are synonymous. A race shares the same culture: that’s Israel. The same history: Israel again. Israel is a race of people, a nation of people. Ancestry is in the Bible, pedigree pertaining to Israel, families, house, and race is in there too.
This chapter is referred to as the table of nations, or the table of races. “Now these are the generations of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth: and unto them were sons born after the flood.”
These are his children. Among the sons of Gomer is Germany. Javan is Greece, and among the sons of Javan are Spain and Rome, and another that is part of Rome also.

“By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.” In their what? In their nations. These three men produced nations: you had Semitic, or as some would say Shemitic, races.

precepts.why: “These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues, in their countries, and in their nations.” In their nations: Ham had nations that came out of him, like Japheth.

“These are the sons of Shem, after their families”: that’s our forefather, “after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.” “These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations”: after their what? After their generations. They generated children. “In their nations”: within their nations.

“And by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood.” The nations were divided. They were never supposed to be together. That is the natural order of things: nations being divided, not being together. God don’t like that. In that time they tried the melting pot, and the Most High confounded the languages during the first melting pot, with Nimrod’s kingdom.

sense.text: “My son, keep the flower of thine age sound”: keep it strong. The flower of your age is your virginity. “And give not thy strength to strangers”: do not give yourself over to heathen women. That is what he’s talking about.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession”: a fruitful possession is a woman, “through all the field”, throughout the land, “sow it with thine own seed”. Your own seed. “Trusting in the goodness of thy stock”: trusting in the goodness of your stock. That word stock was found in genealogy.

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified”. Thy what? Thy race. Your race is in the Bible. The race which you leave behind, your descendants, shall be magnified, “having the confidence of their good descent.” Line of descent, descendant, race, descent: the same thing, in the Bible. This is a prophet speaking to his people.

Race is in the Bible, descent, pedigree, nation. Where do you get that they’re not a race? From fairy tales. Some nations are good at creating fables and fairy tales, like their God.

“So all Israel were reckoned by genealogies”. Reckoned goes back to being acknowledged or considered: Israel was established by genealogies. “And, behold, they were written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, who were carried away to Babylon for their transgression.”

So Israel had what was called a city hall of our own, a Hall of Records among the kings. Our genealogies were found in the records of the kings. Back then you could go to our records and say, I’m from so and so, and they would look you up: yeah, you’re the lineage of so and so. That’s how it was back then.

Guess who has those now? The heathen has those now. We don’t have that no more. Yet you have Israelites saying, oh, you’re a mamser, you’re a bastard, which is comical, very hilarious, to hear that nonsense come out of people’s mouths. That gets dealt with later.

precepts.why: “And the number of them, after their genealogy by their generations, heads of the house of their fathers”. The house of their fathers: genealogy comes from your generation, from the house of your fathers. Israel was numbered that way, “mighty men of valour, was twenty thousand and two hundred.”

sense.text:
Those which went up “could not shew their father’s house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel”. They could not prove their father’s house, their father’s lineage. They could not provide proof, and that shows that Israel had records. We had what they call today birth certificates; Israel had those back then. Some came forward and said, listen, I don’t have any evidence that that’s my forefather. We had records back then of our lineages.

Where it says “their seed”, the margin says pedigree: their seed, or their pedigree, “whether they were of Israel.” So you are considered Israel based upon your father’s house. Not mother’s house: father’s house.

“These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found”: they couldn’t find them in the records. “Therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood.” They were not allowed to do the priest’s office in the temple, because they could not prove that they were Levites.

The one that’s governor there, this is about Nehemiah, said “that they should not eat of the most holy things”: they could not perform the priestly duties, “till there stood up a priest”. Until the Most High comes and speaks to another priest that can confirm that they are Israel. The Most High had to come forward between that and say, listen, these guys are Israelites, and establish it. That was the only way they could determine they were Israel without registry, without record: they had to go to the Lord himself to find out if they were Israel or not.

Unlike today. Our genealogy now is based upon Deuteronomy 28, Deuteronomy 33, 2 Esdras 13, Psalms 83, Joel 3. That’s our Hall of Records now.

precepts.why: The same account, speaking of genealogy, generation and the house of their fathers. “Neither could they shew their families, nor their stock, how they were of Israel”. Their families goes back to family tree, and their stock goes back to genealogy again. They could not show how they were of Israel or not.

“And of the priests that usurped the office of the priesthood, and were not found”: they were in a priestly office, doing the priest’s office, but they couldn’t prove that they were Levites. You can’t prove you’re a Levite, you can’t be in here; we don’t know if you’re Israel or not.

“And when the description of the kindred of these men was sought in the register, and was not found, they were removed from executing the office of the priesthood: For unto them said Nehemias”, that goes back to the governor in Ezra, “that they should not be partakers of the holy things, till there arose up an high priest clothed with doctrine and truth.” Same thing as in Ezra.

Now Nehemiah in his own book. During this time Israel had to rid themselves of the heathen they were following behind. When they came back from Babylon they came back with Babylonian wives, heathen wives and doctrines, and their children were speaking the heathen language with heathen customs. So Nehemiah had to clean house and start over fresh; that’s what’s happening in Nehemiah and Ezra.

“And my God put into mine heart to gather together the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, that they might be reckoned by genealogy. And I found a register of the genealogy of them which came up at the first, and found written therein”, and what he found written there is what was read in Ezra. Nehemiah was the one who discovered the Hall of Records: he found our records, the genealogies of our people who first came up from exile from Babylon.

sense.text: “Now concerning Moses the man of God, his sons were named of the tribe of Levi.” Moses’ sons were named of the tribe of Levi. This is being lined up for a reason.

Moses had two sons. Of the first, one “was the chief”, and of the second, one was “the chief”, and he “had none other sons; but the sons of” that chief “were very many.” He had one son, and that son had a whole bunch of kids. So both sons of Moses were numbered among the tribe of Levi.

“And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.” Why? Because it was against the law, even before Moses, to marry outside of your nation. You weren’t supposed to do that. He married an African woman: Moses, a black man, married a dark woman, a black woman also, but not of the children of Israel.

The bastards say, oh, it was because she was black and Moses was white. No, that’s not why. It’s because she was a Hamite. They were angry because through the tradition of the fathers passed down, you weren’t supposed to do that.

That’s why Moses’ brother and sister, Miriam primarily, were mad as hell: what you marry that for? We supposed to marry our own, passed through tradition. That’s where the anger came from. When Miriam went overboard she got turned to a white girl, went from Miriam to Paris Hilton for like a week.

Through that Ethiopian woman Moses had his two boys, the sons named of Levi. Two sons from an Ethiopian woman, and what tribe were they? Levi, based upon the house of their fathers. But according to some, if your father or mother is a heathen you are a bastard somehow. Yet they’re numbered Levites. Interesting doctrine that is.

precepts.why: Proof that it was the tradition of the fathers. “And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth”: Hamites, like Cush, which would be an Ethiopian woman. “If Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?” If our son Jacob marries a Hamite, I’m be mad as hell. You don’t marry no Hamite; I’ll have no Hamites in this house. That’s what she’s saying.

The next chapter: “And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan”, of Ham. “Arise”, go “to the house of” “thy mother’s father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of” “thy mother’s brother”: your uncle.

And with marrying his own comes the blessing: “And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people; And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee”, your children, “that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger”.

“Jacob obeyed his father and his mother”. Jacob obeyed his parents and went and married a woman of his own kindred. Watch what Esau does: “Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father”, his parents didn’t like that, “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had” “the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son”.

He still didn’t marry his own. Esau was a Hebrew, and he still married something else. Those children were still …, period.

This is why he went and married into Ishmael. “And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of” “the Hittite”, and another, “the daughter of” “the Hittite”: two Hittites, Hamites. He married two Hamite women, “Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.” His parents were pissed: who you married that for?

See how Esau was rebellious. He married three heathen women, and that’s why he’s called a profane fornicator, because he wasn’t supposed to do that. So even before Moses it was a law not to marry outside of your own.

Who the Ethiopian woman was: “And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses” “his daughter.” That’s the Ethiopian woman. The man was Jethro, an Ethiopian priest, a Cushite priest, over Midian. He is often taken for a Midianite because he resided there, but he was a priest over Midian.

“And she bare him a son”, and he named him, “for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.” His name means stranger. He had that son, and the other son from her as well: the two sons numbered of Levi.

sense.text:
Remember why Moses married that woman: he was away from his people for forty years in a foreign land. All of Israel was in Egypt; Moses fled out of Egypt and resided in that area with that man for forty years. Moses wasn’t going to sit there and do nothing, so the Lord let that ride. Likewise Joseph: his family was in Canaan, he was a prisoner in Egypt, eventually he rose to status, and he married what was there, because his family was not there. So he had an excuse.

So brothers trying to use that as an excuse: no. You cannot use Moses or Joseph as an excuse. The Most High let that ride for them.

“And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.” Joseph had two boys, Manasseh the eldest and Ephraim the youngest.

“And now thy two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, which were born unto thee in the land of Egypt before I came unto thee into Egypt, are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine.” Jacob adopted those two into the twelve; they became part of the twelve right here. As Reuben and Simeon are mine, I made these two also part of the twelve.

The dictionary’s mamser is a bastard, a child of incest. That be Moab and Ammon, your so-called wash pots today, the ones who own most of the cleaners and feed us plastic as rice: Chinese, Japanese, that’s them. They’re walking bastards, born of incest, so they’re not allowed in the congregation. A child of a … or a child of adultery is also considered a bastard child, so technically speaking a lot of Israelites be bastards, because a lot of Israelites were born illegitimately. So why would you even use this to condemn other Israelites who have an Israelite father and a heathen mother? Your grandmother or grandfather may have had your father illegitimately as well, and you be a bastard too.

And where it defines a bastard as a mixed population, born of a Jewish father and a heathen mother or vice versa, that would mean Ephraim and Manasseh are bastards and Moses’ children are bastards. And they can’t say that’s after Moses, because it was read that before Moses it was not condoned to intermingle your seed.
“And thy issue, which thou begettest after them, shall be thine, and shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.”

precepts.why: To see who their mother was: “And unto Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim”, by the daughter of the priest of On. Joseph’s wife was Egyptian, another Hamite woman. Just like Moses married a Hamite, Joseph also married a Hamite and had children by her, and these children became the children of Israel. Joseph had Ephraim and Manasseh through an Egyptian woman, and Moses had children counted Levites through an Ethiopian woman.
“Of the tribe of Ephraim”, the son of Nun: of the children of Ephraim.

“These are the names of the men which Moses sent to spy out the land.” And Moses changed the name of the son of Nun to Jehoshua, which means savior, because he was the one that was going to save Israel from the heathen when they got into the promised land. He was the deliverer.

So who became Moses’ successor? Joshua, who happened to have, down the line, an Egyptian great great great great great great great great great great grandmother. And Manasseh too.

sense.text:
Going back further, before Abraham and Isaac. “Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers”: the seed of your fathers is referring to your people. Marry your own people, that’s what he’s saying right there. “And take not a strange woman to wife”: don’t marry another nation, “which is not of thy father’s tribe”, which is not of your people.

There’s another doctrine that states you cannot marry outside your tribe, and they use this: take a wife of your own tribe. But it says here, take a wife of the seed of thy fathers. That confusion gets cleared up too.

“For we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred”. Their own kindred, their own kind, kin: so you can marry your own kin, period. “And were blessed in their children”. It goes back to what was read before: marry your own and your race is magnified, and your children will have the confidence of their good descent.

So the law was to marry within your nation, period. Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob married their own kindred, because they knew back then you had to stay within your lineage. In Noah’s case, the sons of God: his wife was of the sons of God, he stuck with that, and Adam’s line didn’t go outside of that.

Even the conservative scholars in a Bible dictionary, on the flood, hold it: God deals with certain groups, such as the children of Israel, and Noah was not a preacher of righteousness to people of other areas but was concerned with his own people, from which Abraham eventually came. Noah only dealt with his own people and only taught his own people, the sons of God down the line. He didn’t deal with the other nations, the wicked, the daughters of men. He married his own kindred and taught his own kindred only. That goes right back to ‘I’m not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel’: the exact same blueprint, to his own people.

The dictionary’s doctrine is that if both your parents are not Jews, if one of your parents is a heathen, you’re a bastard. Israelites say a Jewish mother makes you Israel. That’s not biblical. If that were the case, Moses’ children should not be counted as Levi, and Ephraim and Manasseh should not be counted in the twelve children of Israel. Jacob would have said, no, I can’t count your kids, the mom’s Egyptian. He said no, they’re mine. Was Jacob the devil? No, he was not.

The reality is you’re only a bastard based upon incest, whoredom, illegitimacy, or being born of a heathen father and a Jewish mother. A heathen father and an Israelite mother is not Israel: that’s a bastard. Not vice versa. An Israelite father and a heathen mother, it’s still Israel. Esau married two Hamite women and still had …; but we marry a heathen woman and it’s a bastard? That don’t make no sense. The rule should apply across the board.

“And Aaron took him” a wife, “daughter of Amminadab”, and she bare him four sons. Aaron took a wife, the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Amminadab’s son. Who is she related to? What tribe was his wife?

The doctrine is that you must only marry your own tribe, you cannot marry outside your tribe. Oh boy, these doctrines. Amminadab is Judah. Amminadab had a son, the prince of Judah, and that son had a sister, and Aaron married her: a Judahite woman. And his children were children of Levi. A high priest came out of that line.

So what happened with ‘you’re supposed to marry within your tribe’? Aaron married a Judahite woman and had Levite children. Joseph married an Egyptian woman and had Israelite children. Moses married an Ethiopian woman and had children of Levi as well. These doctrines are simple and ridiculous.

So you can marry outside the tribe. Why do they push that doctrine? Israel had lands allotted to them. If a man had all daughters and his daughters went off and married into another tribe, who would the land go to? It’s lost to the husband, and that tribe loses that allotment of land. Say Ephraim has a bunch of daughters and they marry Judah; now Judah takes possession of Ephraim’s land. So if a man had a bunch of daughters, they had to marry within the tribe to keep the land allotted within the tribe. That was the instance where it said you must stick to your own tribe; that was when the rule applied.

Here’s the magic question: who in here has land in Israel? No one. You have to have land allotted to you for that rule to apply. And how many of you have a record of your genealogies going back to your tribe? We know by the curses and the attributes given to each tribe who is who today, Deuteronomy 33, Genesis 49, 2 Esdras 13, as far as we can go. But you cannot call anyone a bastard under any circumstance unless you have a record of your genealogy going back as far as Nehemiah and Ezra. A number of our people walking around don’t even know who their father is; who are you to denounce them? And don’t use ancestry.com and have Esau swab your mouth with a Q-tip. Our genealogical record falls upon the curses given to us and the attributes given us: Jacob gave it to us on his deathbed in Genesis 49, Moses in Deuteronomy 33, and 2 Esdras 13. The curses are a clear record. That’s all you need.

precepts.why: “The sons also of Hezron, that were born unto him”, one of them Caleb, of Judah. “And Ram begat Amminadab”: Amminadab was a child of Judah. And Amminadab begat a son, “prince of the children of Judah”. Sound familiar? That son was a prince of the children of Judah, and his sister is the woman Aaron took to wife.
“The sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah”. This chapter is dealing with the sons of Judah, so Hezron, Ram and Amminadab after them are Judah.

Just going to keep nailing it, knocking until it’s gone. “Now these are the generations of” a child of Judah: he “begat Hezron”, “And Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab”, and Amminadab begat the son whose sister is the one Aaron married, and down the line “Boaz begat Obed, And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.” That’s the children of Judah. Aaron married a Judahite.

Clearing it up: the same line from Judah, down through Amminadab, to “Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon”.

So once again: Amminadab had a son, and that son’s sister was Aaron’s wife. So you can marry outside the tribe.

sense.text: We’re going to keep nailing this doctrine that you’re supposed to marry within your tribe. “Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchi–shua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal”. So Saul had two daughters. Watch who the younger one married.

precepts.why:
“And Michal Saul’s daughter loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him.” Now was David a man of the Lord? David could have said, well no, that’s good and all, but I can’t marry you cause you’re not Judah; I can’t marry you, that’s wicked, sis fall back, get off me, don’t sweat me, leave me alone. But he didn’t do that.

“And Saul said, I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” Saul was wicked as hell, cause Saul knew his daughter was evil, and Saul didn’t like David. Saul is saying, take my wicked daughter, take her …. “Wherefore Saul said to David, Thou shalt this day be my son in law in the one of the twain.”

So even though that was Saul’s evil intention, David, being a man of the law, would have known not to marry her if being of another tribe made it wrong. David married her anyway.

“Wherefore David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full tale to the king, that he might be the king’s son in law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.” You understand what Saul did: if you want to marry my daughter, go and kill two hundred Philistines and come back with their foreskins. He was hoping David would get killed. David came back with them: here you go. That was nasty and disgusting, but David loved that sister that much that he did it. Saul was evil, but David loved that sister, and at that moment she did love him, until she went the hell off; she was evil.

But just that shows you that Israel intermarried. Then you read that when Saul was killed, David took Saul’s wives and they became his wives. The tribes intermarried and there was no sin in it.

The only time it was off was when a man had a bunch of daughters. If a man has sons and daughters, he can give his daughter to another tribe, because he has sons to maintain that allotment of land within the tribe. In Numbers there was a man that had a bunch of daughters and no sons, and he was told his daughters were going to marry within his tribe to keep the land within Manasseh. That’s the only instance it’s referring to, the one these fools on YouTube point to, and only because he had daughters.

sense.text:
This is before Moses, once again. Even though you read that it was wrong to marry outside of your own, there were occasions where our forefathers did the wrong things. Not all of our forefathers were holy and perfect and righteous; some of them did foolish things. They were men.

“Judah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah. And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah; and he took her, and went in unto her.”

“She conceived, and bare a son; and he called his name Er.” Then “she called his name Onan”: he was evil too. Then “called his name Shelah”. So Judah had these three boys by a heathen woman. Now let’s see what that last son was: a heathen, or a bastard?

precepts.why: “And the sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Pharez, and Zerah: but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Pharez were Hezron and Hamul.” The son of the Canaanite woman is counted right there among the sons of Judah. And remember Hezron: Amminadab and so forth came from him, and his sister married Aaron.

“And the sons of Judah after their families were; of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites: of Pharez, the family of the Pharzites: of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites.” So he was considered a child of Judah. He was a Judahite. His mom was a Canaanite, but he was still an Israelite. It does not change anything.

If it did, he should not be listed here as Judah; he should be listed under a bastard list. And others should be on that list with him: David should be there. The list goes on and on.

You are who your father is. It’s all throughout the Bible: Numbers 1 makes it clear, families of your fathers, pedigree of your fathers, house of your fathers, over and over and over again.

sense.text:
Now the doctrine is that you can become a Jew through conversion: that the heathens were converted and became Jews, that you can just convert. So you can pretty much subscribe to Hinduism and automatically become East Indian? You can convert to Buddhism and automatically become Chinese? I don’t understand how that works. A religion can’t change a nationality. A nationality is different from a religion; they’re two very different things.

“And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children.” This is when Israel left out of Egypt.

“And a mixed multitude went up also with them”. The heathens saw what our God did to the Egyptians and acknowledged our God, and they said, can we go with you? And it was, hey, come on. The Lord didn’t deliver them; he delivered us. Those nations that were under the Egyptian rule as well, aside from Israel, decided to leave with us. They weren’t saved, but they acknowledged our God and came behind us. “And flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.” Now let’s see what they brought with them.

precepts.why:
The same mixed multitude. Watch what these heathen did after they left with us: “the mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?” The mixed multitude had influence over us, and they were lusting to go back to Egypt.

“We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. The mixed multitude got Israel going: man, remember that Big Mac they had in Egypt, they had McDonald’s, they had freaking Boston Market over there, and we here eating bread and water; this is some bull, this …, Moses brought us in this desert to die.

So the heathen were complaining first, and then they influenced Israel through their complaints. A mixed multitude around us is a problem; that was an issue with us.

When they came out with us, what became of them? Did they become our equals? Did we become brothers in arms? Heathens are trying to dip and dodge like Mayweather to avoid it, but you’re not going to avoid it; it’s inevitable for you. So we’re going to read it for you, cause I know you’re watching.

“Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.” Bondmaids means slaves. “Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.” “And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever”. Forever. That is their purpose: to be our bondmen and bondwomen forever.

I said it a long time ago and I say it again: the nations today are slaves on the loose. They’re like a wild dog running around; their master’s lost and they’re running around doing all kind of wild stuff. But eventually we’re going to get the leash again and put you right back on it. That’s the end result for you; just embrace it, it’s okay.

“But over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour”. The heathen were going to be serving in harder bondage. We had Hebrew servants, menservants and handmaids: those were our own people, and we didn’t give them hard labor. But the heathens we gave hard labor. That’s the difference. There was a bias in that, because y’all ain’t us.

So when the nations that were serving in bondage under the Egyptians came out along with us, having seen the plagues and the wonders and miracles the Lord did for us, they became our bondmen and bondwomen, not our equals and buddies and pals. They became possessions, an inheritance; when they died, their children became our possession, perpetual slaves. That was their purpose. And while they were living in our land they were following our rules, doing what we wanted them to do in order to stay there. They were our tenants, pretty much.

sense.text:
Now let’s go to the magic scripture they use. What the so-called Jew Israeli does today is say, well, see, in Esther 8 they became Jews, so you can become a Jew. No. When our bondmen and bondwomen became Jews, it means they followed our laws and customs. They became Jews by our ways, by religion, not by nationality.

To bring you up to speed: an Edomite was once again trying to kill us off the earth. The Most High turned the tables on him and he ended up getting killed, and we celebrate that. In the place of the Edomite who tried to kill us off, the Most High put our brother, our Benjamite brother, and Esther was the queen under the king. So the king had Israelites basically as second rulers over the kingdom of Persia. Israel was pretty much ruling under the Persian regime; we had power.

There were two conditions in which Israel would bring the laws to other nations or influence other nations. The first is when Israel was ruling and our influence spread, and nations wanted to follow behind it. We had power, and we had slaves that came under our regime, among us, that had to keep our laws. You can’t be among us eating pork and shrimp; that can’t happen. As long as you remain among us you abide by our laws and rules, and you could stay among us, but they are our servants. This is that instance: Israel was in power again.

“And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.” He was put under the king, second under the king.

“The Jews had light, and gladness, and joy, and honour. And in every province, and in every city, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. And many of the people of the land became Jews”. Why? “For the fear of the Jews fell upon them.” That’s why. We had liberty to keep our laws under the king, because Esther was queen and our brother was second under the king, basically king number two. So out of fear of us the nations said, listen, we’re going to follow your laws then, cause they were afraid of us. We had power at that time. Likewise when we came out of Egypt, we had power at that time.

The second instance where Israel let the heathen learn our laws is when Israel was in exile. We were living among ourselves and keeping our laws among ourselves, and the heathen would watch us and go, wow, look how they conduct themselves among each other, we want to do that. So to keep the peace we would share our wisdom with the other nations among us, so that all nations within that area would learn how to keep the laws and there would be no confusion in the land: no pagans, no idols, everyone in the same land mass doing the same thing.

Muhammad saw how the Jews conducted themselves and wanted to learn how we conduct ourselves. We said fine and gave understanding. What did Muhammad do? Turned against us. A lot of us fled into the areas of Turkey and resided among another people there, also as a minority; they saw how we live and wanted to follow that, and we said okay, here you go. What did they do? They turned against us and became Jews, became us all of a sudden. That’s what the heathen do. Another example on this side of the world: the pilgrims. Israel on this side of the world showed them how to live here and survive, how to cultivate the land. Here you go; thanks; they killed us, took over: you guys go to the reservation over there. Same exact thing. We always kick ourselves in the behind. The Bible says never trust your enemies, and a lot of Israel did not follow that.

Those are the two instances where Israel would share their wisdom among the nations. When we were in the majority and ruling, and Jerusalem was expanding, the nations had to either convert, or get put out, or get killed out of the land. Only when we had power, or when we were at our lowest, would we share our wisdom with other nations. When we had power it was beneficial; when we didn’t, it bit us in the behind in the end. In this instance we had power, and in the instance of Exodus 12, when the heathen, the mixed multitude, came out with us, we had power also.

precepts.why:
“Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Jews had rule over them that hated them;)”. The Jews had rule over them that hated them. So when the Jews had rule over them that hated them, the nations were forced to follow our ways, and then they’re referred to as having become Jews. Their ways, the heathen ways, were converted to our ways: that’s what it means when it says they became Jews. They didn’t become ethnically Jews; they didn’t become racially Jews. By their ways and traditions they became Jews.

Herod was an Edomite, but he was a Jew: an Edomite Jew. He was not an Israelite, but he followed our ways, well, sort of.
“Now it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.” They did. We got rid of the mixed multitude; they were causing too many problems.

That law still applies even now: remove yourself from the other nations. “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. The unclean thing is the nations and their customs. Touch not the unclean thing.

sense.text:
“It shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills”. That goes to Israel being on top, ruling over them that hate them, the way it was in Esther. The difference is you won’t have Persia, a nation, over us; we’ll be the top nation. During the time of Esther, even though we had rule, the Persians were the dominant empire; that was their empire. We were given rulership over everybody else because Esther was queen and our brother was second to the king, but we were still under a foreign nation’s dominion. In this instance Israel is above “the top of the mountains”, meaning other nations, and “exalted above the hills”, meaning smaller nations: above all nations, once again, the way we were predestined to be.

“And all nations shall flow unto it.” You may think it’s talking about all heathen nations. It’s referring to our own nation, and we’re going to prove it.

“And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law”. Out of Zion shall go forth the law, meaning order, “and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

“And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks”. They is us. We’re going to beat the other nations’ weapons into cultivating instruments. They’re going to go from fighting against us to servants; pruning instruments are used to cultivate land, to work: from warriors to workers. “Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.”

“O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.” That’s talking about all Israel right there. So again we’re reading about Israel coming together, being established above all nations, and forcing the nations to serve the laws of God.

precepts.why: To prove that “all nations shall flow unto it”: “For there shall be a day, that the watchmen upon the mount Ephraim shall cry, Arise ye, and let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God.” See that: the watchmen upon mount Ephraim shall cry, arise, let us go up to Zion. Then back to Isaiah 2:3: “Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob”. It is Israel going up.

“In those days, and in that time, saith the Lord, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together, going and weeping: they shall go, and seek the Lord their God. They shall ask the way to Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come, and let us join ourselves to the Lord in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten.” The children of Israel and the children of Judah together: “Come, and let us join ourselves to the Lord”. It’s saying the exact same thing again as Isaiah 2:3.

“And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto thee.” Read in the same line as the people going up to Zion to join themselves to the Lord.

This explains what “all nations shall flow unto it” is. “For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he”: the heathens. “Therefore they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow together to the goodness of the Lord”. What do they do? Flow together. The house of Jacob shall flow together, to the goodness of the Lord, “for wheat, and for wine, and for oil, and for the young of the flock and of the herd: and their soul shall be as a watered garden; and they shall not sorrow any more at all.” No more captivity. So the flowing together is referring to the redeemed of Jacob.

sense.text: Let’s show you out of Christ’s own mouth, cause there ain’t going to be no kumbaya with all the nations coming together; whoever ain’t Israel is going to bow down. “But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.” We have the understanding that we’re Israel, and we got to hold fast and keep the commandments till Christ returns. But there’s people on YouTube trying to take that away from us; that’s why he says hold it fast till I come. You’re a stupid negro if you let some dumb people that don’t understand the Bible make you question your ethnicity and your connection to the Most High.

“And he that overcometh”: because we got to overcome our sins, ourselves, the things that are in the world, our family members, the wicked people around us. “And keepeth my works unto the end”: because the campaign now on YouTube is to make you stop the works, and the number one target is IUIC. Don’t listen to them; they’re liars. We’ve exposed them; we show you the twelve tribes chart. They say we’re marrying heathen. They go through the audience in our videos and photos and look at anybody that’s light-skinned and say they’re white. They took a picture of me and my daughter and said I got a heathen wife; they took my daughter’s picture and said that’s my wife, you stupid Negroes. They hate Hispanics, they hate the northern kingdom. They’re trying to stop us from keeping these works until the end.

“To him will I give power over the nations”. If we’re all equal, why would Christ promise us power over the nations? This is our Christ’s mouth, your Savior. We wouldn’t need power over the nations if we were all equal and all kumbaya together.

So when we get that power, what are we going to do? “And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”: we’re going to use a rod of iron to rule over them. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: we’re going to break them into serving our God, because they got a lot of mouth right now, a lot of beliefs, a lot of gods, a lot of talk. That’s why I don’t do a lot of talking now; I’m waiting for this day to come, so anybody that don’t listen can get their behind beat. Glory in thinking about that day. “Even as I received of my Father”: the Most High is going to give his Son power, and he says, I’m going to give it to you, and we’re going to whoop people’s behinds.

In the same vein. “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”. The spirit itself is this Bible bearing witness with our spirit. When we read the Bible, we read the curses and the conditions of the people within this book, and you know that’s talking about us. No other nation can relate to that: the lynchings, the hangings, separating from your family, the slave ships. No other nation can relate to that. It doesn’t bear witness with their spirit; it’s not for them. That’s heavy.

“Our” is for us. That’s not for everybody; it don’t say with all nations. How did all the other nations magically become children of God now? Because you’re listening to idiots that hate you break the Bible down. They realize, if you can’t beat them, join them, so they want to join us by saying we’re Israelites, we’re part of God’s kingdom also.

So the we and the our are the Jews he’s writing to in Romans 1:7, 2:17 and 7:1, that know the law. He’s writing to Jews in Rome.

“And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”. If we’re the children of God, then we are heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, “if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.” When you are a joint heir you receive what’s called a joint inheritance. So what did the Messiah receive as an inheritance?

precepts.why: See who he’s talking to. “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Stop. For I speak to them that know the law. Who is he talking to? And when he comes back to it: so he’s talking to Jews. I speak to them that know the law, so he’s speaking to the Jews that resided in Rome.

Going to the very beginning of the book: “To all that be in Rome”. Stop. Remember it’s a letter to the Romans, right? So he’s talking to Edom, right? Let’s see: “beloved of God, called to be saints”. Called to be what? Called to be saints.

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. Who? Even of the children of Israel. So the saints are the children of Israel, and the ones in Rome “called to be saints” are the children of Israel.

“Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. I thought Paul was writing to Romans? Thou callest thyself a Jew: he’s writing to Jews in Rome. Where do you get Edomite Romans from? Thou callest thyself a Jew and restest in the law.

When you read the last chapter of Acts, it explains that Paul is in Rome, talking to the Israelites in Rome. He sent letters to them while on house arrest in Rome, to the synagogues in Rome.

This goes in conjunction with Revelation 2:25. The nations want to be part of Israel? We’re going to help you become part of us; we’ll show you how they’re going to do it. “Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion. I will declare the decree: the Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.” This is the Messiah speaking through David, saying what the Lord said to him in the heavens.

“Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance”. For thine what? Inheritance. So if we’re joint heirs, what do we get? The heathen, like in Leviticus 25:44: you’re bondmen for how long? Forever. “And the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession”: the planet for your possession.

“Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron”: same thing Christ said: they’re going to get their behinds whooped. “Thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” That’s what the Lord said to us in Revelation: if you overcome, you’ll receive that pleasure; you’ll be joint heirs of that. So where is the equality in that?

sense.text: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.” The strangers are going to cleave: they’re going to keep the laws.

“And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids.” “And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were”: we shall take them captives whose captives we were. “And they shall rule over their oppressors”: we shall rule over our oppressors, with a rod of iron. If they try to pop off, they’re going to be dashed into pieces, and we’ll take great joy in doing it too.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” He’s going to give you rest from your sorrow, from your fear, and from the hard bondage you were made to serve in. Remember that: you’ll be free from that.

Now rumor has it that this happened already, and they use Ezra to say so. They’re thirsty for knowledge and want to teach you; we’re going to help them out with what it means. Read Ezra and Nehemiah side by side and it’s plain: in Ezra’s time we were still servants, still bondmen, still in distress under the kings of Persia. That is not Isaiah 14. Isaiah 14 is rest, no more bondage, and Israel ruling over its oppressors with the nations brought to our place. It has not happened yet.

precepts.why:
This is the verse they use to say Isaiah 14 happened already: “Beside their servants and their maids, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred thirty and seven: and there were among them two hundred singing men and singing women.” They say, see, that’s Isaiah 14: the nations are under them right here in Ezra.

But Ezra was during the Persian captivity. The oppressors were still over us. And those servants and maids were our own people, not the other nations. We had servants and maids already during that time in Persia; that doesn’t make it freedom, and it’s not what Nehemiah says about that same exact time.

Who was with Ezra during his time? Nehemiah. He was Ezra’s contemporary; they were among each other. So let’s see what Nehemiah said about the condition of Israel when those servants and maids were among us. Maybe Nehemiah and Ezra are different spirits. Maybe Nehemiah was the devil the Bible speaks of.

“For they have not served thee in their kingdom”: we did not serve the Lord in our own kingdom, “neither turned they from their wicked works.”

“Behold, we are servants this day.” Isaiah 14 says we’ll be free from that: we’ll rule over our oppressors, have rest, and bring the nations to our place. But here, during Ezra’s time, Nehemiah says we are servants this day. “And for the land that thou gavest unto our fathers to eat the fruit thereof and the good thereof, behold, we are servants in it”: servants, slaves, in our own land.

“And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins.” That’s not what Isaiah 14 says. “Also they have dominion over our bodies.” What is that called? That’s called slavery. “And over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” Not great rest: great distress.

So how could that be Isaiah 14 fulfilled? If we were free during that time, why is Nehemiah saying this? That Isaiah 14 don’t make no damn sense. That’s not Isaiah 14 fulfilled. Stop talking, you sound stupid. Stay out of the Bible.

They say we were established then, that’s when we got freedom, that’s when we were allowed to do whatever we wanted. Let’s see what the Bible says. “Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled”: Jeremiah had already prophesied that this was going to happen.

“The Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia.” So it wasn’t that Israel broke free from the Persians and got what they wanted. It was prophesied that the Lord was going to ease them up off of us a little bit. “Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”: so he was still ruling. He had everything shut down, but the Lord put the spirit on him. “And he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah”: he wanted a house built for the Israelites in Jerusalem.

“Who is there among you of all his people?” He asked who among the Israelites that still believe in the Most High wants to go back and rebuild, “and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” Everything was taken from us. It was already in prophecy that God was going to put it on the heart of the kings to let the Israelites have a place to worship. The heart of the kings is in God’s hands; he can easily make the kings do whatever he wants.

It wasn’t that we were free and could do whatever we wanted. There were plenty of times, even now, that he allowed the kings of the earth to give us certain liberties so we could build the nation of Israel again. It’s the same with Israel United in Christ: if you left it up to the other nations, they wouldn’t let us wear purple, get a building, or teach our people the laws. But the Lord put it on their hearts; certain freedoms and certain laws were put in place so that they would ease up and let these people build. The same thing you see in Ezra is what’s happening with us now. They were not free.

Nehemiah said we are servants this day; see what Ezra says. “And now for a little space grace hath been shewed from the Lord our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and give us a little reviving in our bondage.” A little bit of leniency while in our captivity, a little reviving in our bondage: that’s what Ezra is saying. That’s not what Isaiah 14 says. Isaiah 14:3 is rest “from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.”

“For we were bondmen; yet our God hath not forsaken us in our bondage, but hath extended mercy unto us in the sight of the kings of Persia”: Cyrus, Darius. “To give us a reviving, to set up the house of our God”: that’s the little reviving while in our bondage. Through the Persian kings the Most High gave us the break to rebuild the second temple, “and to repair the desolations thereof, and to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem,” which Nehemiah was behind the construction of.

They were still in captivity in this verse. There’s no confusion: it’s not referring to Isaiah 14. Stop using that.

sense.text:
These heathens are trying their best to make America appear as if we’re free here. You’re free as long as you’re on the bottom and believe in white jesus, and you can all become a Jew, because a Jew, they say, is not a race of people.

“Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the Lord.”

“Ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew”: the skirt is the bottom of your garment. “Saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.” They will have seen the Most High bring America to destruction and put us on top of all nations, ruling, and they’re going to come by: listen, we want to serve your God too.

There ain’t going to be no ‘you can be a convert, we be converts together.’ That ain’t in the Bible. You ain’t converting nothing. The one thing that’s going to be converted is you going from free to slave: that’s the only conversion you’re going to get.

So we’re not playing games with y’all; you cannot come with these doctrines that Jews ain’t a race of people. When you say that, you’re denying who the Messiah came to save. If he came for his people, and his people are not a race of people, then that opens the door for everybody. Y’all ain’t slick; we see through it. That’s why we’re the target: we come out the Bible and smash you each time. And I attack Christianity every chance I get; I’m going to burn every Christianity bridge I can find, and anybody that’s coming against us.
“And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.” When Israel is set up above the mountains and above the hills, nations are going to come to us.

This goes back to Zechariah 8, where they grab the skirt of the Jew. “All they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side.” We’re going to have remnants of our people from foreign lands brought over by the heathens.

“Then thou shalt see, and flow together.” Remember that term, flow together: who’s flowing together? Judah and Ephraim.

“Because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee.” The abundance of the seas is the ships. The nations are all going to come together equally with all their wealth and bring it to you equally. Arabs have gold, Ammon has gold, Moab: they’re all going to put the gold on their ships equally and bring it to us.

“The multitude of camels shall cover thee”: the dromedaries are the one-hump camels. “All they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the Lord.” They’re going to bring honor to our kingdom.

“The rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee”: not with bombs. With gold and incense, that’s what they’re going to bring. “They shall come up with acceptance on mine altar, and I will glorify the house of my glory.”

“Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far, their silver and their gold with them.” We have our children in foreign lands, still scattered, who know who they are, and the heathen know they’re Israel. They’re going to bring them: listen, you’re Israel, you got to go, you can’t be here no more, get out of here, go to your people. “Unto the name of the Lord thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he hath glorified thee.”
“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: equally. “And their kings shall minister unto thee”: equally. “For in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.”

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night.” Why? “That men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the wealth of the Gentiles. We’re going to have our gates open all the time, with all kinds of gold and silver and brass and clothing and silk, expensive things brought into our kingdom back to back, all day long. We’re going to be the wealthiest kingdom on the planet, with everyone’s wealth in our kingdom, because it’s really ours anyway.

“And that their kings may be brought”: we’re going to have their kings brought to us in chains too. That’s part of the forces.

“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” See, that privilege goes to all nations. Here you go, equality: you don’t serve us, you’re going to get put to death.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together”: wood, “to beautify the place of my sanctuary”: decorated. “And I will make the place of my feet glorious.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet.” There’s your privilege right there. Those of you online, the friends, the enemies, heathens alike: you get to bow down to us equally. Congratulations. That bowing down is the best part.

“And they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel”: everybody is going to know where Israel is at that point.
“Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated”: we have been forsaken and hated, “so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.”

“Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings”: that means take all their resources, like they did to us. Suck them dry, so nothing’s left, and they’ve got to keep bringing it; just keep taking their wealth, take their forces.

“And thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer”: not everyone’s Saviour and Redeemer. Thy Saviour, thy Redeemer, “the mighty One of Jacob.”

“For brass I will bring gold”: no more brass for you, you’re going to replace your brass with gold. “And for iron I will bring silver”: the things that are iron in your houses, no more of that; you want gold, you want silver. “And for wood brass, and for stones iron.”

“I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness”: we’re going to have our own people collecting tax and tribute from the other nations.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: no more black-on-black crime, no more violence in our land from the other nations. Is violence being heard in that Israel today? Yes it is, so it ain’t talking about them. “Wasting nor destruction within thy borders”: there’s been war going on since they got in the land, and the Bible says no more war.

“But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation”: within the walls of our land, that will be salvation. So when someone says to you ‘I’m saved,’ ask where. If you’re here, you ain’t saved, because the walls are salvation: where we are, in our kingdom, with our walls built up by the heathens.

precepts.why:
Out of Christ’s mouth, the same bowing down. “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan”: the devils. There’s a church on this earth right now that is filled with devils, “which say they are Jews, and are not.” We’ve got people lying about who the real Jews are, and that’s who Christ said he’s going to target upon his return: “but do lie.” You’ve got liars out there.

“Behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet”: that’s just what we read in Isaiah 60. When Christ comes, he’s going to make whoever’s lying come and bow down before the real Jews’ feet.

“And to know that I have loved thee,” because you’re confused about who Christ loves. When he comes, he’s going to make it clear who he loves. You people want to listen to the white man, to the foolishness, to the scholars with the degrees; we listen to our spirit, because it bears witness. That’s what we’re waiting on: Christ is going to make these pastors bow down before your feet, and you’re going to be like, damn, Jesus does love me, like the Bible says. Y’all sing that song, ‘Jesus loves me, this I know’: we ain’t going to have to sing that song. You’re going to know he loves you when the other nations are bowing before your feet. That’s love. Get out of that Christian state of mind, that foolishness.

sense.text:
They’re trying to get us to believe that the impostors over there in Jerusalem are the real Jews. They’re in Tel Aviv. Do you know they have alarm systems throughout Tel Aviv, and when the alarm goes off the people have to run, because the Arabs are shooting rockets over the walls? Does that sound like people God is protecting? Does that sound like people God has freed and delivered, the chosen people of God? How could you live, if at any time you can look up and see a rocket coming to hit your house? That don’t make no damn sense.

The freedom the Bible gives to the Israelites, that the Deacon just explained: we’re going to be chilling. We’re going to wake up, ‘Yo, how many slaves you got?’ ‘I got more slaves than you.’ ‘Where your wife at?’ ‘She’s out there picking our stuff,’ because you know how Eve is, how the Israelite women are: they love to decorate, they love to shop. That’s what you’re going to be doing. We ain’t going to be punching in from nine to five and getting peanuts; all the stuff you’re comfortable with now is going to stop. This is going to be like, this is what I’m supposed to be doing: ruling.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: there shall be no rockets flying over your walls. If what’s over there is prophecy fulfilled, it don’t make no sense. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.” God is going to be right there with us; the Messiah is going to be sitting in the kingdom, right in there with us.

“Thy sun shall no more go down.” No more ‘what’s that scripture again, I can’t remember, where is that verse’: no more of that. It’s going to be all in here; you’re going to know everything and not forget nothing.

“For the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.” That’s the rest without fear; it goes back to Isaiah 14.

precepts.why:
Let’s see if it goes in conjunction with Isaiah 60, or if it’s talking about now. “And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.” That’s Isaiah 60.

“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it”: Israel. “And the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”: that’s the nations, Isaiah 60. “And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there. And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it”: that’s what we read in Isaiah 60.

That’s prophecy, and this has not happened yet at all. The Arabs are not trying to bring no damn gold to that Israel. They’re trying to bring a bomb: gold with C4 taped to the bottom of it, ‘I bring you a gift from Allah,’ boom.
